summary.title: How to Write a Git Commit Message
summary.one_liner: Learn the seven rules for writing clear Git commit messages: a short imperative subject line, a blank line, a wrapped body that explains what and why rather than how.
keywords: blank line between subject and body
explain why not how in commits
writing git commits like a pro
takeaways: Separate the commit subject from the body with a blank line; tools like log, shortlog and rebase depend on it.
Keep the subject line to about 50 characters (72 as a hard limit), capitalized, without a trailing period.
Write the subject in the imperative mood, so it completes the sentence 'If applied, this commit will ...'.
Wrap the body at 72 characters and use it to explain what and why rather than how, since the code shows how.
summary.summary: The article argues that most Git logs are messy and that a consistent commit message convention makes history far more useful for review, blame, revert and maintenance. It presents seven rules (blank line after subject, 50-character subject, capitalization, no trailing period, imperative mood, 72-character body wrap, and explaining what and why) with examples drawn from Spring, Git's own generated messages, Bitcoin Core and a Tron-themed sample. It also gives tips on using the command line over an IDE for Git and recommends reading the free Pro Git book.
